title: Women's experiences of resettlement from prison and domestic abuse
official: Prison, resettlement and domestic abuse: a qualitative study to explore women's experiences and needs to enhance practice and policy
summary:
Background and study aims
Many women in prison have experienced domestic abuse. After leaving prison, they may face challenges such as finding safe housing, getting a job, accessing health and support services, and rebuilding their lives. Some women do not receive the emotional and practical support they need, which can increase the risk of further abuse or returning to prison.

This study aims to understand the experiences of women who have experienced domestic abuse and are resettling into the community after leaving prison. The researchers want to learn about the support women need, what helps them most, and what barriers they face. The findings will be used to improve services, guide good practice, and help inform future policy and care for women in similar situations.

Who can participate?
The study is recruiting women aged 18 years and over who have been in prison within the last two years and have experienced domestic abuse in the past. Participants must not currently be experiencing domestic abuse and must not have experienced domestic abuse within the previous six months.

The study will also involve policymakers, service providers and professionals who work in criminal justice, domestic abuse and social care services.

What does the study involve?
Women taking part will join a research project that uses photographs and group discussions to help them share their experiences. This approach, known as Photovoice, allows people to express thoughts and experiences that may be difficult to describe in words alone.

Participants will take part in a series of five half-day workshops held in groups. During these sessions, they will use photographs and discussion to explore their experiences of leaving prison and rebuilding their lives after domestic abuse. Researchers will listen to their views and experiences to better understand the challenges they face and the support they need.

Some women with personal experience of prison and domestic abuse will also receive training to become peer researchers and help carry out the study.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants may benefit from having the opportunity to share their experiences and contribute to research that could improve support services for women leaving prison after domestic abuse. The findings may help organisations develop better services and support systems in the future.

However, discussing past experiences of domestic abuse and imprisonment may be upsetting or emotionally difficult for some participants. The study uses photographs and supported group discussions to help participants communicate experiences in a way that may feel more comfortable.

Where is the study run from?
The study is run from the University of Sheffield, Sheffield, United Kingdom. Recruitment and study activities will take place in several regions, including Greater Manchester, London, Yorkshire and Humberside, and Wales.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
The study began recruiting participants on 1 July 2026. Recruitment is expected to continue until 30 June 2027, and the study is expected to finish on 30 November 2027.

Who is funding the study?
The study is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR).

Who is the main contact?
Prof Michaela Rogers

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
WP2: Women aged 18 years+ with experience of prison during the last two years (WP2) and with experience of DVA but not current or recent DVA (within the last six months)
WP3: Policymakers, service providers and professionals working in criminal justice, domestic abuse and social care
Exclusion criteria:
WP2: Women currently or very recently (within the last six months) in abusive situations, aged 17 years and under
WP3: Professionals who have not had direct experience of working with women with DVA and prison experience or who have no experience of working in policy/campaigning relevant to the field
